title: Annotatio II §.II: Babylonian Captivity Deus est homo parallel; Musculus absolves personal union
pass_a_gloss: On the other hand, in On the Babylonian Captivity Tom. 2 at my p. 265 he compares the Union of bread and Christ’s Body in the Eucharist with the Union of Christ’s human nature and His divine person in such a way that he seems to have made it altogether like that; yet because Luther himself denies the latter, personal, mode of Union in express words in his Greater Confession on the Supper; and in On the Babylonian Captivity, about to refute pontifical Transubstantiation and build the bread’s presence in the Supper, he is found to have instituted only a bare comparison between these two propositions — This, or this bread is my body, and God is man — and to have wished to show how in both a Disparate is predicated of a Disparate; (on which account among our people also Wolfgang Musculus absolves Luther from a personal Union of Christ’s body and blood, Common Places p. m. 354.)
pass_b_english: In On the Babylonian Captivity he compares bread–body union with the hypostatic union (Deus est homo), which looks personal.

Yet his Greater Confession on the Supper denies a personal mode, and the Captivity comparison is only bare Disparate-of-Disparate predication — so Musculus (among ours) absolves him from personal union of body and blood.
source_text: Ex altera parte, Unionem panis & Corporis Christi in Eucharistia cum Unione humanae Christi naturae, & personae ejus divinae, in libro de Captivitate Babylonica Tom. 2. mihi p. 265. eum in modum comparat, ut huic per omnia similem fecisse visus sit; tamen, quia tum ipse Lutherus posteriorem Unionis modum, seu personalem, conceptis verbis in Confessione sua majore de Coena, negat; in Libro autem de Captivitate Babylonica, Transsubstantiationem pontificiam refutaturus, panisque in Coena praesentiam adstructurus, inter propositiones has duas: Hoc, seu, hic panis est corpus meum, Et, Deus est homo, nudam duntaxat earum comparationem instituisse deprehenditur & ostendere gestivisse, quô modô utrobique Disparatum de Disparato praedicetur; (Quô nomine etiam inter nostrates Wolfgangus Musculus, Lutherum à personali corporis & sanguinis Christi Unione absolvit Loci commun. p. m. 354.)

choices.english: a disparate predicated of a disparate
